"""Execution programs have a phase structure: early same-sign runs with rising participation can continue, while late runs with declining participation are more likely inventory exhaustion. This factor explicitly distinguishes acceleration in run length and volume participation from a mature price trend, rather than treating every momentum observation identically. It is falsified if the conditional return distribution does not differ between accelerating and decelerating same-sign runs of comparable cumulative size."""

from __future__ import annotations

import numpy as np
import pandas as pd

from quant_fund_agent.factors.base import BaseFactor
from quant_fund_agent.factors.ops import rank
from quant_fund_agent.factors.registry import register_factor


def _run_phase_statistics(
    direction: pd.DataFrame,
    log_abnormal_volume: pd.DataFrame,
    directional_extreme: pd.DataFrame,
) -> tuple[pd.DataFrame, pd.DataFrame, pd.DataFrame]:
    """Causally accumulate current signed-run length, volume slope, and conviction.

    Each run is reset whenever return sign changes or is zero.  Within a live
    run, the volume slope is the expanding OLS slope of log abnormal volume on
    event time (1, 2, ..., run length), and conviction is the running fraction
    of bars closing near the directional extreme.
    """
    index = direction.index
    columns = direction.columns
    sign_values = direction.fillna(0.0).to_numpy(dtype=float)
    volume_values = log_abnormal_volume.fillna(0.0).to_numpy(dtype=float)
    extreme_values = directional_extreme.fillna(0.0).to_numpy(dtype=float)

    n_rows, n_cols = sign_values.shape
    run_length = np.zeros((n_rows, n_cols), dtype=float)
    volume_slope = np.zeros((n_rows, n_cols), dtype=float)
    extreme_fraction = np.zeros((n_rows, n_cols), dtype=float)

    length = np.zeros(n_cols, dtype=float)
    sum_x = np.zeros(n_cols, dtype=float)
    sum_xx = np.zeros(n_cols, dtype=float)
    sum_y = np.zeros(n_cols, dtype=float)
    sum_xy = np.zeros(n_cols, dtype=float)
    extreme_count = np.zeros(n_cols, dtype=float)
    previous_sign = np.zeros(n_cols, dtype=float)

    for t in range(n_rows):
        current_sign = sign_values[t]
        valid = current_sign != 0.0
        continuing = valid & (current_sign == previous_sign)
        restarting = valid & ~continuing

        next_x = length + 1.0
        length = np.where(continuing, next_x, np.where(restarting, 1.0, 0.0))
        sum_x = np.where(continuing, sum_x + next_x, np.where(restarting, 1.0, 0.0))
        sum_xx = np.where(
            continuing,
            sum_xx + next_x * next_x,
            np.where(restarting, 1.0, 0.0),
        )
        sum_y = np.where(
            continuing,
            sum_y + volume_values[t],
            np.where(restarting, volume_values[t], 0.0),
        )
        sum_xy = np.where(
            continuing,
            sum_xy + next_x * volume_values[t],
            np.where(restarting, volume_values[t], 0.0),
        )
        extreme_count = np.where(
            continuing,
            extreme_count + extreme_values[t],
            np.where(restarting, extreme_values[t], 0.0),
        )

        denominator = length * sum_xx - sum_x * sum_x
        slope = np.divide(
            length * sum_xy - sum_x * sum_y,
            denominator,
            out=np.zeros(n_cols, dtype=float),
            where=denominator != 0.0,
        )
        fraction = np.divide(
            extreme_count,
            length,
            out=np.zeros(n_cols, dtype=float),
            where=length > 0.0,
        )

        run_length[t] = length
        volume_slope[t] = slope
        extreme_fraction[t] = fraction
        previous_sign = current_sign

    return (
        pd.DataFrame(run_length, index=index, columns=columns),
        pd.DataFrame(volume_slope, index=index, columns=columns),
        pd.DataFrame(extreme_fraction, index=index, columns=columns),
    )


@register_factor
class ExecutionRunPhaseTransition(BaseFactor):
    """Directional execution-run continuation versus inventory-exhaustion signal."""

    factor_id = "run_length_volume_phase_transition"
    name = "Execution Run Phase Transition"
    category = "momentum"
    description = (
        "Ranks signed return runs by their causal abnormal-volume acceleration "
        "and directional close-location conviction, fading mature runs when "
        "participation and conviction deteriorate."
    )
    window_length = 40
    inputs = ["close", "high", "low", "volume"]
    prediction_horizon = 6
    suggested_horizons = [6]

    def calc(self, data: dict[str, pd.DataFrame]) -> pd.DataFrame:
        close = data["close"].ffill().fillna(0.0)
        high = data["high"].fillna(close)
        low = data["low"].fillna(close)
        volume = data["volume"].fillna(0.0).clip(lower=0.0)

        ret = close.pct_change().replace([np.inf, -np.inf], np.nan).fillna(0.0)
        direction = np.sign(ret)

        prior_volume_mean = volume.rolling(20, min_periods=5).mean().shift(1)
        abnormal_volume = volume / prior_volume_mean.replace(0.0, np.nan)
        log_abnormal_volume = np.log(abnormal_volume.clip(lower=0.05, upper=20.0))
        log_abnormal_volume = log_abnormal_volume.replace([np.inf, -np.inf], np.nan).fillna(0.0)

        bar_range = (high - low).abs().replace(0.0, np.nan)
        close_location = ((close - low) / bar_range).clip(lower=0.0, upper=1.0).fillna(0.5)
        directional_extreme = pd.DataFrame(
            np.where(
                direction.to_numpy() > 0.0,
                (close_location.to_numpy() >= 0.75).astype(float),
                np.where(
                    direction.to_numpy() < 0.0,
                    (close_location.to_numpy() <= 0.25).astype(float),
                    0.0,
                ),
            ),
            index=close.index,
            columns=close.columns,
        )

        run_length, volume_slope, extreme_fraction = _run_phase_statistics(
            direction,
            log_abnormal_volume,
            directional_extreme,
        )

        participation = pd.DataFrame(
            np.tanh(1.5 * volume_slope.to_numpy()),
            index=close.index,
            columns=close.columns,
        )
        conviction = 2.0 * extreme_fraction - 1.0
        run_quality = participation + conviction
        maturity = (run_length / 8.0).clip(lower=0.0, upper=1.0)

        continuation = run_quality.clip(lower=0.0) * (1.0 - 0.35 * maturity)
        exhaustion = (-run_quality).clip(lower=0.0) * maturity
        raw_signal = direction * (continuation - exhaustion)

        active_run = run_length >= 2.0
        return rank(raw_signal.where(active_run)).where(active_run, 0.0).fillna(0.0)

"""Daily volume shocks are imperfect marks of latent order-flow events, but their spacing contains information beyond total volume: a directional shock following a quiet refractory interval is more likely to represent newly arrived information, whereas an equally large shock inside a tightly clustered burst is more likely to reflect saturated execution and inventory transfer. The factor goes with sparse, renewed directional pressure and against dense, rapidly recurring pressure after controlling for range and volume magnitude. It would fail if event spacing adds no incremental forecast beyond signed return and volume; persistence can survive because execution schedules, investor attention, and dealer inventory constraints create different price-impact regimes that are difficult to identify from a single bar."""

from __future__ import annotations

import numpy as np
import pandas as pd

from quant_fund_agent.factors.base import BaseFactor
from quant_fund_agent.factors.ops import rank
from quant_fund_agent.factors.registry import register_factor


def _same_sign_waiting_times(
    positive_events: pd.DataFrame, negative_events: pd.DataFrame
) -> pd.DataFrame:
    """Return event-time gaps since the prior event with the same return sign.

    The row loop updates all tickers simultaneously and only carries prior
    event timestamps forward, making the construction strictly causal.
    """
    pos = positive_events.to_numpy(dtype=bool)
    neg = negative_events.to_numpy(dtype=bool)
    n_rows, n_cols = pos.shape

    gaps = np.full((n_rows, n_cols), np.nan, dtype=float)
    last_positive = np.full(n_cols, -1, dtype=int)
    last_negative = np.full(n_cols, -1, dtype=int)

    for t in range(n_rows):
        pos_now = pos[t]
        neg_now = neg[t]

        prior_pos = last_positive[pos_now]
        prior_neg = last_negative[neg_now]

        if pos_now.any():
            pos_cols = np.flatnonzero(pos_now)
            valid_pos = prior_pos >= 0
            gaps[t, pos_cols[valid_pos]] = t - prior_pos[valid_pos]
            last_positive[pos_cols] = t

        if neg_now.any():
            neg_cols = np.flatnonzero(neg_now)
            valid_neg = prior_neg >= 0
            gaps[t, neg_cols[valid_neg]] = t - prior_neg[valid_neg]
            last_negative[neg_cols] = t

    return pd.DataFrame(gaps, index=positive_events.index, columns=positive_events.columns)


@register_factor
class EventTimeRefractoryPressureSplit(BaseFactor):
    """Renewed directional volume events versus saturated same-sign bursts."""

    factor_id = "event_time_refractory_pressure_split"
    name = "Event-Time Refractory Pressure Split"
    category = "microstructure"
    description = (
        "Ranks directional high-participation events by whether their same-sign "
        "waiting time is unusually long or unusually short relative to the "
        "stock's recent event-time distribution."
    )
    window_length = 80
    inputs = ["close", "high", "low", "volume"]
    prediction_horizon = 6
    suggested_horizons = [6]

    def calc(self, data: dict[str, pd.DataFrame]) -> pd.DataFrame:
        close = data["close"]
        high = data["high"]
        low = data["low"]
        volume = data["volume"]

        valid_bar = (
            close.notna()
            & high.notna()
            & low.notna()
            & volume.notna()
            & (close > 0.0)
            & (volume > 0.0)
        )

        previous_close = close.shift(1).replace(0.0, np.nan)
        ret = (close / previous_close - 1.0).replace([np.inf, -np.inf], np.nan)

        # Log-volume innovations identify unusually high participation without
        # allowing raw share volume to dominate the cross section.
        log_volume = np.log(volume.where(volume > 0.0))
        vol_mean = log_volume.rolling(20, min_periods=12).mean()
        vol_std = log_volume.rolling(20, min_periods=12).std().replace(0.0, np.nan)
        vol_z = ((log_volume - vol_mean) / vol_std).replace([np.inf, -np.inf], np.nan)
        event = ((vol_z > 1.0) & valid_bar).fillna(False)

        # Close-location and range-normalised return form a bounded directional
        # pressure mark, so a wide but indecisive bar is not treated as strong
        # directional information.
        bar_range = (high - low).replace(0.0, np.nan)
        close_location = ((2.0 * close - high - low) / bar_range).clip(-1.0, 1.0)
        relative_range = (bar_range / previous_close.abs()).replace(0.0, np.nan)
        directional_efficiency = (ret.abs() / relative_range).clip(0.0, 1.0)
        pressure = (np.sign(ret) * close_location.abs() * directional_efficiency)
        pressure = pressure.where(valid_bar, 0.0).fillna(0.0)

        positive_events = (event & (ret > 0.0)).fillna(False)
        negative_events = (event & (ret < 0.0)).fillna(False)
        waiting_time = _same_sign_waiting_times(positive_events, negative_events)

        # The shifted rolling median is the event-time refractory benchmark
        # known before the current event.  Gaps are observed only on events,
        # so the median is naturally an event-time rather than calendar-time
        # distribution estimate.
        typical_wait = waiting_time.rolling(60, min_periods=4).median().shift(1)
        renewal_score = np.log(waiting_time / typical_wait.replace(0.0, np.nan))
        renewal_score = renewal_score.replace([np.inf, -np.inf], np.nan).clip(-2.0, 2.0)
        renewal_score = renewal_score.where(event, 0.0).fillna(0.0)

        # Positive renewed buying is followed; positive buying inside a dense
        # burst is faded.  The same logic applies symmetrically to selling.
        raw_signal = (pressure * renewal_score).where(event, 0.0).fillna(0.0)
        return rank(raw_signal).fillna(0.5)

The factor goes with sparse, renewed directional pressure and against dense, rapidly recurring pressure after controlling for range and volume magnitude. """Order-flow excitation can be temporarily hidden when repeated high-volume bars are absorbed within a narrowing price range. Compression despite elevated participation suggests a queueing or inventory-transfer regime; the eventual escape should occur in the direction of the accumulated close-location imbalance, particularly when the firm has no adverse fundamental deterioration. The idea is rejected if compressed high-participation episodes break randomly after conditioning on signed close location and fundamental state."""

from __future__ import annotations

import numpy as np
import pandas as pd

from quant_fund_agent.factors.base import BaseFactor
from quant_fund_agent.factors.ops import rank
from quant_fund_agent.factors.registry import register_factor


def _compression_score(high: pd.DataFrame, low: pd.DataFrame, close: pd.DataFrame) -> pd.DataFrame:
    """Causal multiscale contraction of percentage intrabar ranges."""
    safe_close = close.abs().replace(0.0, np.nan)
    bar_range = ((high - low).clip(lower=0.0) / safe_close).replace([np.inf, -np.inf], np.nan)

    short_5 = bar_range.rolling(5, min_periods=3).mean()
    medium_10 = bar_range.rolling(10, min_periods=5).mean()
    base_30 = bar_range.rolling(30, min_periods=15).mean().replace(0.0, np.nan)
    base_60 = bar_range.rolling(60, min_periods=30).mean().replace(0.0, np.nan)

    relative_range = 0.5 * (short_5 / base_30 + medium_10 / base_60)
    return (1.0 - relative_range).clip(lower=0.0, upper=1.0).fillna(0.0)


def _excitation_imbalance(
    high: pd.DataFrame,
    low: pd.DataFrame,
    close: pd.DataFrame,
    volume: pd.DataFrame,
) -> tuple[pd.DataFrame, pd.DataFrame]:
    """Exponentially decayed marked-event intensity and its signed imbalance.

    High abnormal-volume bars are treated as events.  The mark is the close
    location in the bar, and the exponential kernel is the discrete-time
    Hawkes-style memory of recent order-flow excitation.
    """
    log_volume = np.log1p(volume.clip(lower=0.0).fillna(0.0))
    volume_mean = log_volume.rolling(20, min_periods=10).mean()
    volume_std = log_volume.rolling(20, min_periods=10).std().replace(0.0, np.nan)
    abnormal_volume = ((log_volume - volume_mean) / volume_std).clip(lower=0.0, upper=5.0).fillna(0.0)

    bar_width = (high - low).clip(lower=0.0).replace(0.0, np.nan)
    close_location = ((2.0 * close - high - low) / bar_width).clip(lower=-1.0, upper=1.0).fillna(0.0)

    # ewm(alpha) / alpha is proportional to the recursive kernel
    # lambda_t = mark_t + decay * lambda_(t-1), using only present and past bars.
    alpha = 1.0 - 0.5 ** (1.0 / 4.0)
    activity = abnormal_volume.ewm(alpha=alpha, adjust=False, min_periods=1).mean() / alpha
    signed_activity = (abnormal_volume * close_location).ewm(
        alpha=alpha, adjust=False, min_periods=1
    ).mean() / alpha

    persistence = (signed_activity / activity.replace(0.0, np.nan)).clip(lower=-1.0, upper=1.0).fillna(0.0)
    intensity = (activity / activity.rolling(60, min_periods=20).mean().replace(0.0, np.nan)).clip(
        lower=0.0, upper=3.0
    ).fillna(0.0)
    return intensity, persistence


def _fundamental_state(eps_estimate: pd.DataFrame, free_cash_flow: pd.DataFrame) -> pd.DataFrame:
    """Slow point-in-time estimate/cash-flow condition; unavailable data is neutral."""
    eps_lag = eps_estimate.shift(63)
    eps_change = (eps_estimate - eps_lag) / (eps_lag.abs() + 0.05)
    eps_change = eps_change.replace([np.inf, -np.inf], np.nan).clip(lower=-2.0, upper=2.0)

    fcf_lag = free_cash_flow.shift(63)
    fcf_scale = free_cash_flow.abs().rolling(126, min_periods=20).median().replace(0.0, np.nan)
    fcf_change = ((free_cash_flow - fcf_lag) / fcf_scale).replace([np.inf, -np.inf], np.nan)
    fcf_change = fcf_change.clip(lower=-2.0, upper=2.0)

    available = eps_change.notna().astype(float) + fcf_change.notna().astype(float)
    improvement = (eps_change.fillna(0.0) + fcf_change.fillna(0.0)) / available.replace(0.0, np.nan)
    improvement = improvement.fillna(0.0)

    # Stable names receive a permissive gate; deterioration suppresses breakout pressure.
    return (0.75 + 0.25 * np.tanh(1.5 * improvement)).clip(lower=0.25, upper=1.0)


@register_factor
class RangeCompressionExcitationEscape(BaseFactor):
    """Directional breakout pressure from compressed, excited order flow."""

    factor_id = "range_compression_excitation_escape"
    name = "Range Compression Excitation Escape"
    category = "volatility"
    description = (
        "Cross-sectional directional breakout score for names with multiscale "
        "range compression, decayed abnormal-volume excitation, persistent "
        "signed close-location imbalance, and stable-to-improving fundamentals."
    )
    window_length = 126
    inputs = ["high", "low", "close", "volume", "epsEstimate", "freeCashFlow"]
    prediction_horizon = 6
    suggested_horizons = [6]

    def calc(self, data: dict[str, pd.DataFrame]) -> pd.DataFrame:
        close = data["close"].fillna(0.0)
        high = data["high"].fillna(close)
        low = data["low"].fillna(close)
        volume = data["volume"].fillna(0.0)
        eps_estimate = data["epsEstimate"]
        free_cash_flow = data["freeCashFlow"]

        compression = _compression_score(high, low, close)
        intensity, imbalance = _excitation_imbalance(high, low, close, volume)
        fundamental_gate = _fundamental_state(eps_estimate, free_cash_flow)

        raw_signal = compression * intensity * imbalance * fundamental_gate
        return rank(raw_signal.replace([np.inf, -np.inf], np.nan).fillna(0.0)).fillna(0.5)

"""Directional abnormal-volume shocks often cluster because institutional execution, stop activation, and attention create self-exciting sequences rather than isolated observations. A fresh shock has continuation value when the estimated excitation process is active but still subcritical: there is evidence of a cascade, without the late-stage saturation that tends to exhaust liquidity and reverse. The mechanism is falsified if continuation is equally strong after estimated branching intensity is near or above one, where the proposed headroom distinction should matter."""

from __future__ import annotations

import numpy as np
import pandas as pd

from quant_fund_agent.factors.base import BaseFactor
from quant_fund_agent.factors.ops import rank
from quant_fund_agent.factors.registry import register_factor


def _exponential_event_intensity(events: pd.DataFrame, decay: float) -> pd.DataFrame:
    """Causal unnormalised exponential Hawkes-style event state."""
    values = events.fillna(0.0).to_numpy(dtype=float, copy=True)
    values[~np.isfinite(values)] = 0.0
    intensity = np.zeros_like(values, dtype=float)

    for t in range(values.shape[0]):
        if t == 0:
            intensity[t] = values[t]
        else:
            intensity[t] = values[t] + decay * intensity[t - 1]

    return pd.DataFrame(intensity, index=events.index, columns=events.columns)


def _branching_proxy(
    events: pd.DataFrame,
    pre_event_intensity: pd.DataFrame,
    decay: float,
    window: int,
) -> pd.DataFrame:
    """Trailing OLS kernel-mass estimate from event response to prior state.

    If event probability responds as a * prior exponential state, the
    exponentially decaying kernel has integrated branching mass a/(1-decay).
    All moments are trailing and the explanatory state is lagged one bar.
    """
    x = pre_event_intensity.shift(1).fillna(0.0)
    y = events.fillna(0.0)

    mean_x = x.rolling(window, min_periods=window).mean()
    mean_y = y.rolling(window, min_periods=window).mean()
    mean_xy = (x * y).rolling(window, min_periods=window).mean()
    mean_x2 = (x * x).rolling(window, min_periods=window).mean()

    covariance = mean_xy - mean_x * mean_y
    variance = mean_x2 - mean_x * mean_x
    slope = covariance / variance.where(variance > 1.0e-12, np.nan)
    return slope / (1.0 - decay)


@register_factor
class SubcriticalMarkedShockBranchingHeadroom(BaseFactor):
    """Ranks directional marked shocks only in active subcritical cascades."""

    factor_id = "subcritical_marked_shock_branching_headroom"
    name = "Subcritical Marked-Shock Branching Headroom"
    category = "momentum"
    description = (
        "Defines signed return shocks jointly confirmed by abnormal volume and "
        "intraday range, then ranks their marked exponential intensity only "
        "when a trailing Hawkes-style branching estimate is positive, active, "
        "and below a saturation cutoff."
    )
    window_length = 60
    inputs = ["close", "high", "low", "volume"]
    prediction_horizon = 6
    suggested_horizons = [6]

    def calc(self, data: dict[str, pd.DataFrame]) -> pd.DataFrame:
        close = data["close"].replace(0.0, np.nan)
        high = data["high"].replace(0.0, np.nan)
        low = data["low"].replace(0.0, np.nan)
        volume = data["volume"].replace(0.0, np.nan)

        ret = close.pct_change(fill_method=None)
        intraday_range = ((high - low).abs() / close.abs()).replace(
            [np.inf, -np.inf], np.nan
        )

        shock_window = 20
        ret_mean = ret.rolling(shock_window, min_periods=shock_window).mean()
        ret_std = ret.rolling(shock_window, min_periods=shock_window).std()
        ret_z = ((ret - ret_mean) / ret_std.where(ret_std > 1.0e-12, np.nan)).replace(
            [np.inf, -np.inf], np.nan
        )

        vol_mean = volume.rolling(shock_window, min_periods=shock_window).mean()
        vol_std = volume.rolling(shock_window, min_periods=shock_window).std()
        vol_z = ((volume - vol_mean) / vol_std.where(vol_std > 1.0e-12, np.nan)).replace(
            [np.inf, -np.inf], np.nan
        )

        range_mean = intraday_range.rolling(
            shock_window, min_periods=shock_window
        ).mean()
        range_std = intraday_range.rolling(
            shock_window, min_periods=shock_window
        ).std()
        range_z = (
            (intraday_range - range_mean)
            / range_std.where(range_std > 1.0e-12, np.nan)
        ).replace([np.inf, -np.inf], np.nan)

        confirmed = (vol_z > 1.0) & (range_z > 1.0) & (ret_z.abs() > 1.25)
        positive_events = ((ret_z > 1.25) & confirmed).astype(float).fillna(0.0)
        negative_events = ((ret_z < -1.25) & confirmed).astype(float).fillna(0.0)
        all_events = (positive_events + negative_events).clip(lower=0.0, upper=1.0)

        decay = 0.80
        positive_intensity = _exponential_event_intensity(positive_events, decay)
        negative_intensity = _exponential_event_intensity(negative_events, decay)
        total_intensity = positive_intensity + negative_intensity

        branching = _branching_proxy(all_events, total_intensity, decay, 40)
        signed_intensity = positive_intensity - negative_intensity

        # A positive but modest kernel mass indicates ongoing contagion with
        # remaining headroom; near-critical cascades are excluded as exhausted.
        active_subcritical = (branching > 0.10) & (branching < 0.85)
        signal = rank(signed_intensity).where(active_subcritical, 0.0)
        return signal.replace([np.inf, -np.inf], np.nan).fillna(0.0)

"""Persistent institutional execution tends to arrive on a relatively regular participation schedule, whereas isolated news or liquidity shocks create more irregular volume bursts. A directional bar accompanied by unusually predictable recent volume-clock behavior is more likely to represent unfinished execution and continue over the next week. The hypothesis is falsified if signed returns following regular-volume directional shocks are no more persistent than returns following equally large irregular-volume shocks."""

from __future__ import annotations

import numpy as np
import pandas as pd

from quant_fund_agent.factors.base import BaseFactor
from quant_fund_agent.factors.ops import rank
from quant_fund_agent.factors.registry import register_factor


def _volume_clock_regularity(
    normalized_volume: pd.DataFrame,
    window: int,
) -> pd.DataFrame:
    """Trailing regularity of normalized volume arrivals.

    Combines inverse coefficient of variation with normalized entropy of volume
    participation weights. Both quantities use only the trailing window: a
    stable participation schedule has low dispersion and high entropy, while a
    one-off burst has high dispersion and concentrated low-entropy weights.
    """
    rolling_mean = normalized_volume.rolling(window, min_periods=window).mean()
    rolling_std = normalized_volume.rolling(window, min_periods=window).std()
    coefficient_variation = rolling_std / rolling_mean.replace(0.0, np.nan)
    inverse_cv = 1.0 / (1.0 + coefficient_variation.clip(lower=0.0))

    volume_sum = normalized_volume.rolling(window, min_periods=window).sum()
    weights = normalized_volume / volume_sum.replace(0.0, np.nan)
    entropy_terms = -(weights.where(weights > 0.0) * np.log(weights.where(weights > 0.0)))
    entropy = entropy_terms.rolling(window, min_periods=window).sum()
    normalized_entropy = entropy / np.log(float(window))

    regularity = 0.5 * inverse_cv + 0.5 * normalized_entropy.clip(lower=0.0, upper=1.0)
    return regularity.clip(lower=0.0, upper=1.0)


@register_factor
class ArrivalClockRegularityFollowthrough(BaseFactor):
    """Continuation score for directional moves with regular volume-clock arrivals."""

    factor_id = "arrival_clock_regularity_followthrough"
    name = "Regular Volume-Clock Follow-Through"
    category = "microstructure"
    description = (
        "Cross-sectional continuation score that favors directional bars with "
        "unusually elevated but regular trailing volume participation, measured "
        "from normalized-volume dispersion and arrival entropy."
    )
    window_length = 60
    inputs = ["close", "high", "low", "volume"]
    prediction_horizon = 6
    suggested_horizons = [6]

    def calc(self, data: dict[str, pd.DataFrame]) -> pd.DataFrame:
        close = data["close"]
        high = data["high"]
        low = data["low"]
        volume = data["volume"]

        safe_volume = volume.fillna(0.0).clip(lower=0.0)
        volume_baseline = safe_volume.rolling(60, min_periods=20).mean()
        normalized_volume = safe_volume / volume_baseline.replace(0.0, np.nan)
        normalized_volume = normalized_volume.replace([np.inf, -np.inf], np.nan)

        regularity = _volume_clock_regularity(normalized_volume, 20)
        volume_shock = normalized_volume.clip(lower=0.0, upper=3.0)

        prior_close = close.shift(1)
        signed_return = (close / prior_close.replace(0.0, np.nan) - 1.0)
        signed_return = signed_return.replace([np.inf, -np.inf], np.nan)

        price_range = (high - low).replace(0.0, np.nan)
        close_location = ((2.0 * close - high - low) / price_range).clip(-1.0, 1.0)
        close_location = close_location.replace([np.inf, -np.inf], np.nan)

        directional_conviction = signed_return * close_location
        score = directional_conviction * volume_shock * regularity
        score = score.replace([np.inf, -np.inf], np.nan).fillna(0.0)
        return rank(score).fillna(0.5)

"""The same daily range can reflect informed trading or temporary liquidity pressure. A directional move that closes near the extreme and achieves large range per unit of abnormal volume suggests scarce opposing liquidity and informed price discovery; a move with large volume but poor close location suggests absorption and likely reversal. The premise is rejected if close-location-conditioned range efficiency does not distinguish continuation from absorbed-flow reversals."""

from __future__ import annotations

import numpy as np
import pandas as pd

from quant_fund_agent.factors.base import BaseFactor
from quant_fund_agent.factors.ops import rank
from quant_fund_agent.factors.registry import register_factor


def _directional_efficiency_surprise(
    efficiency: pd.DataFrame,
    lookback: int,
    min_observations: int,
) -> pd.DataFrame:
    """Score signed efficiency against prior same-direction trailing samples."""
    positive = efficiency.where(efficiency > 0.0)
    negative_magnitude = (-efficiency).where(efficiency < 0.0)

    # Shifted distributions ensure the current bar is evaluated only against
    # information available before its own price-discovery outcome.
    prior_positive = positive.shift(1)
    prior_negative = negative_magnitude.shift(1)

    up_mean = prior_positive.rolling(
        lookback, min_periods=min_observations
    ).mean()
    up_std = prior_positive.rolling(
        lookback, min_periods=min_observations
    ).std()
    down_mean = prior_negative.rolling(
        lookback, min_periods=min_observations
    ).mean()
    down_std = prior_negative.rolling(
        lookback, min_periods=min_observations
    ).std()

    up_surprise = (positive - up_mean) / up_std.replace(0.0, np.nan)
    down_surprise = (negative_magnitude - down_mean) / down_std.replace(
        0.0, np.nan
    )

    # A surprising efficient upward discovery is positive; an equivalently
    # strong downward discovery is negative.  Near-zero close location carries
    # no directional discovery signal.
    directional = up_surprise.where(efficiency > 0.0, -down_surprise)
    return directional.clip(lower=-6.0, upper=6.0)


@register_factor
class AsymmetricRangeVolumePriceDiscovery(BaseFactor):
    """Ranks directional range efficiency relative to prior same-side discoveries."""

    factor_id = "asymmetric_range_volume_price_discovery"
    name = "Asymmetric Range-Volume Price Discovery"
    category = "microstructure"
    description = (
        "Cross-sectional rank of close-location-conditioned logarithmic range "
        "per unit of abnormal volume, scored against separate trailing upside "
        "and downside efficiency distributions."
    )
    window_length = 60
    inputs = ["close", "high", "low", "volume"]
    prediction_horizon = 6
    suggested_horizons = [6]

    def calc(self, data: dict[str, pd.DataFrame]) -> pd.DataFrame:
        close = data["close"].astype(float)
        high = data["high"].astype(float)
        low = data["low"].astype(float)
        volume = data["volume"].astype(float).fillna(0.0).clip(lower=0.0)

        bar_range = (high - low).where((high > low) & high.notna() & low.notna())
        close_location = (
            (2.0 * close - high - low) / bar_range.replace(0.0, np.nan)
        ).clip(lower=-1.0, upper=1.0)

        price_scale = close.abs().replace(0.0, np.nan)
        log_range = np.log1p(bar_range / price_scale).clip(lower=0.0)

        # Use a prior trailing median rather than contemporaneous volume to
        # identify abnormal participation without letting the current bar set
        # its own benchmark.  Clipping prevents sparse-volume observations from
        # dominating the cross-section solely through a tiny denominator.
        prior_volume_median = volume.shift(1).rolling(20, min_periods=10).median()
        abnormal_volume = volume / prior_volume_median.replace(0.0, np.nan)
        abnormal_volume = abnormal_volume.clip(lower=0.25, upper=8.0)

        efficiency = (close_location * log_range) / abnormal_volume
        efficiency = efficiency.where(volume > 0.0, 0.0)

        surprise = _directional_efficiency_surprise(
            efficiency, lookback=60, min_observations=12
        )
        return rank(surprise).fillna(0.5)

"""Industry peers often incorporate a common information shock before a slower-moving constituent, particularly when the lagging name has lower recent trading participation or a noisier own-price path. Estimate directed information flow from leave-one-out industry returns into each stock's next-day return state, then trade the contemporaneous peer impulse only when the stock has historically been a receiver rather than a leader. The other side is passive liquidity providers and investors treating the stock-specific move as idiosyncratic; the hypothesis is falsified if receiver classifications do not predict subsequent catch-up after controlling for industry returns."""

from __future__ import annotations

import numpy as np
import pandas as pd

from quant_fund_agent.factors.base import BaseFactor
from quant_fund_agent.factors.ops import rank
from quant_fund_agent.factors.registry import register_factor


def _return_states(ret: pd.DataFrame, volatility_window: int) -> pd.DataFrame:
    """Convert returns into causal signed-magnitude states in {-2, ..., 2}."""
    volatility = ret.rolling(volatility_window, min_periods=10).std()
    scaled = ret / volatility.replace(0.0, np.nan)

    states = pd.DataFrame(0.0, index=ret.index, columns=ret.columns)
    states = states.mask((scaled > 0.35) & (scaled <= 1.25), 1.0)
    states = states.mask(scaled > 1.25, 2.0)
    states = states.mask((scaled < -0.35) & (scaled >= -1.25), -1.0)
    states = states.mask(scaled < -1.25, -2.0)
    return states.where(scaled.notna())


def _conditional_mutual_information(
    target: pd.DataFrame,
    source_lagged: pd.DataFrame,
    target_lagged: pd.DataFrame,
    window: int,
    min_observations: int,
) -> pd.DataFrame:
    """Rolling I(target; source_lagged | target_lagged), using plug-in counts.

    All count estimates are trailing-window estimates.  The discrete source,
    target, and conditioning variables each take five signed-magnitude states.
    """
    valid = target.notna() & source_lagged.notna() & target_lagged.notna()
    observations = valid.astype(float).rolling(window, min_periods=min_observations).sum()
    denominator = observations.replace(0.0, np.nan)
    states = (-2.0, -1.0, 0.0, 1.0, 2.0)

    condition_counts: dict[float, pd.DataFrame] = {}
    target_condition_counts: dict[tuple[float, float], pd.DataFrame] = {}
    source_condition_counts: dict[tuple[float, float], pd.DataFrame] = {}

    for condition_state in states:
        condition_event = valid & target_lagged.eq(condition_state)
        condition_counts[condition_state] = (
            condition_event.astype(float).rolling(window, min_periods=min_observations).sum()
        )

        for target_state in states:
            event = condition_event & target.eq(target_state)
            target_condition_counts[(target_state, condition_state)] = (
                event.astype(float).rolling(window, min_periods=min_observations).sum()
            )

        for source_state in states:
            event = condition_event & source_lagged.eq(source_state)
            source_condition_counts[(source_state, condition_state)] = (
                event.astype(float).rolling(window, min_periods=min_observations).sum()
            )

    information = pd.DataFrame(0.0, index=target.index, columns=target.columns)
    for condition_state in states:
        p_condition = condition_counts[condition_state] / denominator
        for target_state in states:
            p_target_condition = (
                target_condition_counts[(target_state, condition_state)] / denominator
            )
            for source_state in states:
                triple_event = (
                    valid
                    & target_lagged.eq(condition_state)
                    & target.eq(target_state)
                    & source_lagged.eq(source_state)
                )
                triple_count = triple_event.astype(float).rolling(
                    window, min_periods=min_observations
                ).sum()
                p_triple = triple_count / denominator
                p_source_condition = (
                    source_condition_counts[(source_state, condition_state)] / denominator
                )

                ratio = (p_triple * p_condition) / (
                    p_target_condition * p_source_condition
                ).replace(0.0, np.nan)
                contribution = p_triple * np.log(ratio.where(ratio > 0.0))
                information = information + contribution.fillna(0.0)

    return information.clip(lower=0.0).where(observations >= min_observations)


def _leave_one_out_industry_returns(
    ret: pd.DataFrame, industry: pd.DataFrame
) -> pd.DataFrame:
    """Compute equal-weighted contemporaneous peer returns excluding each name."""
    labels = industry.ffill().iloc[-1].copy()
    fallback = pd.Series(ret.columns, index=ret.columns, dtype=object)
    labels = labels.where(labels.notna(), fallback)

    peer_returns = pd.DataFrame(np.nan, index=ret.index, columns=ret.columns)
    for label in pd.unique(labels):
        positions = np.flatnonzero(labels.to_numpy() == label)
        if len(positions) < 2:
            continue

        members = ret.iloc[:, positions]
        member_total = members.fillna(0.0).sum(axis=1)
        member_count = members.notna().sum(axis=1).astype(float)

        for position in positions:
            own_return = ret.iloc[:, position]
            peer_count = member_count - own_return.notna().astype(float)
            peer_total = member_total - own_return.fillna(0.0)
            peer_returns.iloc[:, position] = peer_total / peer_count.replace(0.0, np.nan)

    return peer_returns


@register_factor
class DirectedInformationIndustryLagBridge(BaseFactor):
    """Directed peer-information catch-up signal for industry laggards."""

    factor_id = "directed_information_industry_lag_bridge"
    name = "Directed Industry Information Bridge"
    category = "statistical_arbitrage"
    description = (
        "Discretizes stock and leave-one-out industry returns into signed "
        "magnitude states, estimates rolling conditional mutual information "
        "from lagged peers to the stock conditional on its own lag, subtracts "
        "the reverse leader flow, and ranks the current peer impulse scaled "
        "by the resulting receiver score."
    )
    window_length = 140
    inputs = ["close", "industry"]
    prediction_horizon = 6
    suggested_horizons = [6]

    def calc(self, data: dict[str, pd.DataFrame]) -> pd.DataFrame:
        close = data["close"].where(data["close"] > 0.0)
        stock_returns = close.pct_change(fill_method=None).replace([np.inf, -np.inf], np.nan)
        peer_returns = _leave_one_out_industry_returns(stock_returns, data["industry"])

        stock_states = _return_states(stock_returns, 20)
        peer_states = _return_states(peer_returns, 20)

        forward_flow = _conditional_mutual_information(
            stock_states,
            peer_states.shift(1),
            stock_states.shift(1),
            120,
            90,
        )
        reverse_flow = _conditional_mutual_information(
            peer_states,
            stock_states.shift(1),
            peer_states.shift(1),
            120,
            90,
        )

        receiver_score = (forward_flow - reverse_flow).clip(lower=0.0)
        expected_catch_up = receiver_score * peer_returns
        expected_catch_up = expected_catch_up.where(peer_returns.notna())
        return rank(expected_catch_up).fillna(0.5)

"""Daily directional volume shocks can be treated as marked arrivals: their ability to trigger future same-signed activity depends on both recent self-excitation and remaining liquidity capacity. A positive event with a high estimated branching response but without exhausted range or volume capacity should continue, whereas similarly sized events after a saturated burst should not. The edge is falsified if estimated subcritical versus near-saturated arrival regimes do not differentiate forward signed returns; slow execution schedules and fragmented investor attention provide the economic persistence."""

from __future__ import annotations

import numpy as np
import pandas as pd

from quant_fund_agent.factors.base import BaseFactor
from quant_fund_agent.factors.ops import rank
from quant_fund_agent.factors.registry import register_factor


def _causal_branching_coefficient(
    marks: pd.DataFrame,
    decay_halflife: float,
    estimation_window: int,
) -> tuple[pd.DataFrame, pd.DataFrame]:
    """Estimate a causal marked-arrival branching coefficient and lagged kernel.

    The regression is a trailing, per-name OLS slope of today's non-negative
    mark on an exponentially decayed sum of prior marks.  The one-bar shift in
    the kernel ensures the current event is never used as its own parent.
    """
    alpha = 1.0 - np.exp(np.log(0.5) / decay_halflife)
    lagged_marks = marks.shift(1).fillna(0.0)
    kernel = lagged_marks.ewm(alpha=alpha, adjust=False).mean() / alpha

    mean_mark = marks.rolling(estimation_window, min_periods=estimation_window).mean()
    mean_kernel = kernel.rolling(estimation_window, min_periods=estimation_window).mean()
    covariance = (marks * kernel).rolling(
        estimation_window, min_periods=estimation_window
    ).mean() - mean_mark * mean_kernel
    variance = (kernel * kernel).rolling(
        estimation_window, min_periods=estimation_window
    ).mean() - mean_kernel * mean_kernel

    coefficient = covariance / variance.replace(0.0, np.nan)
    return coefficient.clip(lower=0.0, upper=0.95), kernel


def _marked_arrival_signal(
    close: pd.DataFrame,
    high: pd.DataFrame,
    low: pd.DataFrame,
    volume: pd.DataFrame,
) -> pd.DataFrame:
    """Construct a capacity-adjusted, directional marked-arrival signal."""
    safe_close = close.ffill().fillna(0.0)
    safe_high = high.ffill().fillna(safe_close)
    safe_low = low.ffill().fillna(safe_close)
    safe_volume = volume.fillna(0.0).clip(lower=0.0)

    ret = safe_close.pct_change().replace([np.inf, -np.inf], np.nan).fillna(0.0)
    return_sign = np.sign(ret)

    bar_range = (safe_high - safe_low).abs()
    close_location = (
        2.0 * (safe_close - safe_low) / bar_range.replace(0.0, np.nan) - 1.0
    ).clip(lower=-1.0, upper=1.0).fillna(0.0)
    location_sign = np.sign(close_location)

    log_volume = np.log1p(safe_volume)
    volume_mean = log_volume.rolling(20, min_periods=20).mean()
    volume_std = log_volume.rolling(20, min_periods=20).std()
    volume_surprise = (
        (log_volume - volume_mean) / volume_std.replace(0.0, np.nan)
    ).clip(lower=0.0, upper=4.0).fillna(0.0)

    directional_agreement = 0.5 * (return_sign + location_sign)
    signed_marks = volume_surprise * directional_agreement
    positive_marks = signed_marks.clip(lower=0.0)
    negative_marks = (-signed_marks).clip(lower=0.0)

    beta_pos, kernel_pos = _causal_branching_coefficient(positive_marks, 3.0, 35)
    beta_neg, kernel_neg = _causal_branching_coefficient(negative_marks, 3.0, 35)

    pos_load = kernel_pos + positive_marks
    neg_load = kernel_neg + negative_marks
    pos_normal_load = pos_load.rolling(40, min_periods=20).mean()
    neg_normal_load = neg_load.rolling(40, min_periods=20).mean()

    pos_excess = (pos_load / pos_normal_load.replace(0.0, np.nan) - 1.0).clip(
        lower=0.0, upper=3.0
    )
    neg_excess = (neg_load / neg_normal_load.replace(0.0, np.nan) - 1.0).clip(
        lower=0.0, upper=3.0
    )
    pos_capacity = np.exp(-pos_excess).fillna(1.0)
    neg_capacity = np.exp(-neg_excess).fillna(1.0)

    previous_close = safe_close.shift(1).fillna(safe_close)
    true_range = (safe_high - safe_low).abs()
    high_gap = (safe_high - previous_close).abs()
    low_gap = (safe_low - previous_close).abs()
    true_range = true_range.where(true_range >= high_gap, high_gap)
    true_range = true_range.where(true_range >= low_gap, low_gap)

    short_range = true_range.rolling(5, min_periods=5).sum()
    normal_range = true_range.rolling(40, min_periods=20).mean() * 5.0
    range_excess = (
        short_range / normal_range.replace(0.0, np.nan) - 1.0
    ).clip(lower=0.0, upper=3.0)
    range_capacity = np.exp(-range_excess).fillna(1.0)

    pos_gain = beta_pos / (1.0 - beta_pos).replace(0.0, np.nan)
    neg_gain = beta_neg / (1.0 - beta_neg).replace(0.0, np.nan)
    pos_gain = pos_gain.clip(lower=0.0, upper=8.0).fillna(0.0)
    neg_gain = neg_gain.clip(lower=0.0, upper=8.0).fillna(0.0)

    continuation = (
        positive_marks * pos_gain * pos_capacity
        - negative_marks * neg_gain * neg_capacity
    ) * range_capacity
    return continuation.replace([np.inf, -np.inf], np.nan).fillna(0.0)


@register_factor
class MarkedArrivalBranchingCapacityDrift(BaseFactor):
    """Directional marked-arrival continuation weighted by branching capacity."""

    factor_id = "marked_arrival_branching_capacity_drift"
    name = "Marked Arrival Branching Capacity"
    category = "momentum"
    description = (
        "Ranks signed abnormal-volume arrivals by a causal marked self-excitation "
        "estimate while reducing exposure after same-signed event or range capacity "
        "has been exhausted."
    )
    window_length = 75
    inputs = ["close", "high", "low", "volume"]
    prediction_horizon = 6
    suggested_horizons = [6]

    def calc(self, data: dict[str, pd.DataFrame]) -> pd.DataFrame:
        signal = _marked_arrival_signal(
            data["close"], data["high"], data["low"], data["volume"]
        )
        return rank(signal)

"""A rapid increase in a stock's loading on the dominant cross-sectional return-correlation mode identifies names becoming newly exposed to systematic de-risking before many volatility-targeting and index-oriented investors have fully resized. The signal is bearish for stocks with sharply rising common-mode loadings, especially when their recent return is already negative, and bullish for names whose common-mode exposure is falling. This mechanism should fail if changes in estimated eigenvector loading do not predict subsequent relative returns after controlling for realized volatility; the other side is slow-moving benchmarked capital that adjusts exposure using delayed covariance estimates."""

from __future__ import annotations

import numpy as np
import pandas as pd

from quant_fund_agent.factors.base import BaseFactor
from quant_fund_agent.factors.ops import rank
from quant_fund_agent.factors.registry import register_factor


def _leading_mode_loading(
    ret: pd.DataFrame, window: int, min_observations: int
) -> pd.DataFrame:
    """Causally estimate normalized dominant correlation-eigenvector loadings.

    At each date the correlation matrix uses only the trailing return window.
    Pairwise-missing correlations are set to zero after retaining securities
    with adequate individual observations; this permits a usable eigenspace
    estimate during ordinary panel entry and exit without imputing returns.
    """
    output = pd.DataFrame(np.nan, index=ret.index, columns=ret.columns, dtype=float)
    n_assets = ret.shape[1]

    if n_assets < 3 or len(ret.index) < window:
        return output

    for end in range(window - 1, len(ret.index)):
        sample = ret.iloc[end - window + 1 : end + 1]
        active = sample.count(axis=0) >= min_observations
        active_columns = sample.columns[active]

        if len(active_columns) < 3:
            continue

        corr = sample.loc[:, active_columns].corr(min_periods=min_observations)
        matrix = corr.to_numpy(dtype=float)
        matrix = np.where(np.isfinite(matrix), matrix, 0.0)
        matrix = 0.5 * (matrix + matrix.T)
        np.fill_diagonal(matrix, 1.0)

        try:
            eigenvalues, eigenvectors = np.linalg.eigh(matrix)
        except np.linalg.LinAlgError:
            continue

        leading_vector = eigenvectors[:, -1]
        if np.sum(leading_vector) < 0.0:
            leading_vector = -leading_vector

        # The eigenvector has unit L2 norm.  Scaling by sqrt(N) gives its
        # cross-sectional RMS a stable value of one as universe membership varies.
        normalized_loading = leading_vector * np.sqrt(float(len(active_columns)))
        output.loc[ret.index[end], active_columns] = normalized_loading

    return output


def _range_volatility_scale(
    high: pd.DataFrame, low: pd.DataFrame, window: int, baseline: int
) -> pd.DataFrame:
    """Return a bounded trailing realized-range volatility normalization."""
    safe_high = high.where(high > 0.0)
    safe_low = low.where(low > 0.0)
    log_range = np.log(safe_high / safe_low).replace([np.inf, -np.inf], np.nan)
    log_range = log_range.clip(lower=0.0)

    short_range = log_range.rolling(window, min_periods=max(3, window // 2)).mean()
    long_range = log_range.rolling(baseline, min_periods=max(10, baseline // 2)).mean()
    relative_range = short_range / long_range.replace(0.0, np.nan)

    return np.sqrt(relative_range.clip(lower=0.25, upper=4.0)).fillna(1.0)


@register_factor
class SystematicRiskModeRotation(BaseFactor):
    """Ranks stocks by downside-confirmed rotations into the dominant risk mode."""

    factor_id = "eigenspace_rotation_systematic_unwind"
    name = "Systematic Risk-Mode Rotation"
    category = "statistical_arbitrage"
    description = (
        "Trailing correlation-eigenspace signal that shorts stocks with rising "
        "dominant-mode loadings, particularly after downside confirmation, and "
        "longs stocks rotating away from the common systematic risk mode."
    )
    window_length = 65
    inputs = ["close", "high", "low"]
    prediction_horizon = 6
    suggested_horizons = [6]

    def calc(self, data: dict[str, pd.DataFrame]) -> pd.DataFrame:
        close = data["close"].replace(0.0, np.nan)
        high = data["high"]
        low = data["low"]

        daily_return = close.pct_change(fill_method=None).replace([np.inf, -np.inf], np.nan)
        loading = _leading_mode_loading(daily_return, 45, 30)
        loading_change = loading - loading.shift(5)

        volatility_scale = _range_volatility_scale(high, low, 10, 60)

        recent_return = close.pct_change(5, fill_method=None).replace(
            [np.inf, -np.inf], np.nan
        )
        return_volatility = daily_return.rolling(10, min_periods=5).std()
        downside_confirmation = (
            -recent_return / (return_volatility * np.sqrt(5.0)).replace(0.0, np.nan)
        ).clip(lower=0.0, upper=2.0).fillna(0.0)

        # A rising common-mode loading is bearish.  Negative recent performance
        # strengthens only that systematic-unwind leg; range volatility controls
        # for noisier loading estimates in turbulent names.
        confirmation = 1.0 + downside_confirmation.where(loading_change > 0.0, 0.0)
        signal = -loading_change * confirmation / volatility_scale

        return rank(signal.replace([np.inf, -np.inf], np.nan))

"""A rising sequence of price-range-per-unit-volume readings indicates that progressively less trading is required to move the price, a daily-bar proxy for deteriorating liquidity depth. When this elasticity steepens in the direction of the recent signed close-location pressure, the market is more vulnerable to a continuation jump because marginal liquidity suppliers have withdrawn. The effect should disappear if future range and directional return are unrelated to elasticity curvature after conditioning on ordinary volume and volatility; the other side is liquidity providers and risk managers who reduce quoted risk only gradually."""

from __future__ import annotations

import numpy as np
import pandas as pd

from quant_fund_agent.factors.base import BaseFactor
from quant_fund_agent.factors.ops import rank
from quant_fund_agent.factors.registry import register_factor


def _elasticity_curvature(
    high: pd.DataFrame,
    low: pd.DataFrame,
    close: pd.DataFrame,
    volume: pd.DataFrame,
) -> pd.DataFrame:
    """Causally estimate accelerating log price-impact elasticity."""
    safe_close = close.where(close > 0.0)
    dollar_volume = (safe_close * volume.where(volume > 0.0)).where(lambda x: x > 0.0)

    trailing_median = dollar_volume.rolling(20, min_periods=5).median()
    fallback_floor = safe_close.rolling(20, min_periods=5).median() * 1.0e-6
    volume_floor = (trailing_median * 0.05).combine_first(fallback_floor)
    safe_dollar_volume = dollar_volume.where(dollar_volume >= volume_floor, volume_floor)

    intrabar_range = (high - low).clip(lower=0.0)
    price_floor = safe_close * 1.0e-8
    safe_range = intrabar_range.where(intrabar_range > price_floor, price_floor)
    log_elasticity = np.log(safe_range / safe_dollar_volume)

    short = log_elasticity.rolling(3, min_periods=3).mean()
    medium = log_elasticity.rolling(10, min_periods=7).mean()
    long = log_elasticity.rolling(30, min_periods=15).mean()

    acceleration = (short - medium) - (medium - long)
    curvature_scale = acceleration.rolling(30, min_periods=15).std().replace(0.0, np.nan)
    return acceleration / curvature_scale


def _close_location_pressure(
    high: pd.DataFrame,
    low: pd.DataFrame,
    close: pd.DataFrame,
) -> pd.DataFrame:
    """Trailing signed close-location pressure, bounded against tiny ranges."""
    bar_range = (high - low).clip(lower=0.0)
    price_floor = close.where(close > 0.0) * 1.0e-8
    safe_range = bar_range.where(bar_range > price_floor, np.nan)
    location = ((2.0 * close - high - low) / safe_range).clip(-1.0, 1.0)
    return location.rolling(5, min_periods=3).mean()


@register_factor
class LiquidityElasticityCurvaturePrejump(BaseFactor):
    """Ranks directional acceleration in price-range-per-dollar-volume elasticity."""

    factor_id = "liquidity_elasticity_curvature_prejump"
    name = "Liquidity Elasticity Curvature"
    category = "volatility"
    description = (
        "Estimate daily impact elasticity as intrabar range divided by dollar-volume proxy, "
        "using close times volume with robust floors. Measure the curvature of short-, "
        "medium-, and longer-window elasticity estimates, multiply by recent directional "
        "close location, and rank the resulting signed fragility score cross-sectionally."
    )
    window_length = 60
    inputs = ["high", "low", "close", "volume"]
    prediction_horizon = 6
    suggested_horizons = [6]

    def calc(self, data: dict[str, pd.DataFrame]) -> pd.DataFrame:
        high = data["high"]
        low = data["low"]
        close = data["close"]
        volume = data["volume"]

        curvature = _elasticity_curvature(high, low, close, volume)
        pressure = _close_location_pressure(high, low, close)
        fragility = curvature * pressure

        return rank(fragility).fillna(0.5)

programs.code:
"""A fresh earnings or revenue surprise is more likely to continue when subsequent daily price-volume states become unusually predictable rather than noisy. This is a daily-bar analogue of the low-entropy informed-flow state in the source paper: persistent informed execution makes the sequence of signed returns and relative-volume states compressible, while the surprise supplies the direction that entropy alone cannot identify. The edge should disappear if low-compressibility names do not exhibit larger post-surprise drift than equally surprised but high-compressibility names; arbitrage is limited because the underlying event is sparse and execution urgency is not directly observable."""

from __future__ import annotations

import numpy as np
import pandas as pd

from quant_fund_agent.factors.base import BaseFactor
from quant_fund_agent.factors.ops import rank
from quant_fund_agent.factors.registry import register_factor


def _transition_entropy(close: pd.DataFrame, volume: pd.DataFrame, window: int) -> pd.DataFrame:
    """Causal normalized entropy of trailing return-volume state transitions."""
    ret = close.pct_change(fill_method=None)
    relative_volume = volume / volume.rolling(window, min_periods=10).mean().replace(0.0, np.nan)

    return_state = pd.DataFrame(
        np.where(ret.to_numpy() > 0.0, 2.0, np.where(ret.to_numpy() < 0.0, 0.0, 1.0)),
        index=close.index,
        columns=close.columns,
    )
    volume_state = pd.DataFrame(
        np.where(
            relative_volume.to_numpy() < 0.75,
            0.0,
            np.where(relative_volume.to_numpy() > 1.25, 2.0, 1.0),
        ),
        index=close.index,
        columns=close.columns,
    )

    state = return_state * 3.0 + volume_state
    valid_state = ret.notna() & relative_volume.notna() & volume.notna() & (volume > 0.0)
    valid_transition = valid_state & valid_state.shift(1).fillna(False)
    transition = state.shift(1) * 9.0 + state

    valid_count = valid_transition.astype(float).rolling(window, min_periods=window).sum()
    entropy = pd.DataFrame(0.0, index=close.index, columns=close.columns)

    # There are nine joint bar states and hence 81 possible one-bar transitions.
    # Each rolling count is trailing-only, making the entropy available at t causal.
    for transition_code in range(81):
        count = (
            transition.eq(float(transition_code))
            .where(valid_transition, False)
            .astype(float)
            .rolling(window, min_periods=window)
            .sum()
        )
        probability = count / valid_count.replace(0.0, np.nan)
        entropy = entropy - probability.where(probability > 0.0, 1.0) * np.log(
            probability.where(probability > 0.0, 1.0)
        )

    normalized = entropy / np.log(81.0)
    return normalized.where(valid_count >= float(window))


def _fresh_surprise(current: pd.DataFrame) -> pd.DataFrame:
    """Mark point-in-time surprise observations only when their reported value changes."""
    previous = current.shift(1)
    return current.notna() & (previous.isna() | current.ne(previous))


@register_factor
class CatalystConditionedBarstateCompressibility(BaseFactor):
    """Post-surprise direction weighted by low price-volume transition entropy."""

    factor_id = "catalyst_conditioned_barstate_compressibility"
    name = "Catalyst-Conditioned Bar-State Compressibility"
    category = "sentiment"
    description = (
        "Detects fresh changes in epsSurprise and revenueSurprise, signs them by "
        "the standardized surprise direction, and weights them by low rolling "
        "transition entropy of discretized daily return sign and relative-volume "
        "states. The output is cross-sectionally ranked within date, with stale "
        "or missing fundamental observations suppressed."
    )
    window_length = 21
    inputs = ["close", "volume", "epsSurprise", "revenueSurprise", "epsEstimate", "revenueEstimate"]
    prediction_horizon = 6
    suggested_horizons = [6]

    def calc(self, data: dict[str, pd.DataFrame]) -> pd.DataFrame:
        close = data["close"]
        volume = data["volume"]
        eps_surprise = data["epsSurprise"]
        revenue_surprise = data["revenueSurprise"]
        eps_estimate = data["epsEstimate"]
        revenue_estimate = data["revenueEstimate"]

        eps_fresh = _fresh_surprise(eps_surprise)
        revenue_fresh = _fresh_surprise(revenue_surprise)

        # Scaling by the contemporaneously available consensus makes EPS and
        # revenue surprises dimensionless before they are combined.
        eps_standardized = (
            eps_surprise / eps_estimate.abs().replace(0.0, np.nan)
        ).clip(-5.0, 5.0)
        revenue_standardized = (
            revenue_surprise / revenue_estimate.abs().replace(0.0, np.nan)
        ).clip(-5.0, 5.0)

        eps_component = eps_standardized.where(eps_fresh)
        revenue_component = revenue_standardized.where(revenue_fresh)
        component_count = eps_component.notna().astype(float) + revenue_component.notna().astype(float)
        catalyst_direction = (
            eps_component.fillna(0.0) + revenue_component.fillna(0.0)
        ) / component_count.replace(0.0, np.nan)

        entropy = _transition_entropy(close, volume, 20)
        compressibility = (1.0 - entropy).clip(0.0, 1.0)
        raw_signal = (catalyst_direction * compressibility).where(component_count > 0.0)

        signal = rank(raw_signal)
        return signal.where(raw_signal.notna(), 0.0).fillna(0.0).reindex_like(close)

"""Factor timing is most implementable when the conditional signal is stable enough to avoid excessive turnover, a concern emphasized in the supplied factor-timing study. Cross-sectional quality and valuation signals should be more reliable when market-wide range-per-volume stress is low and cross-sectional return dispersion is moderate, while liquidity-constrained regimes favor defensive balance-sheet characteristics over aggressive growth exposure. The mechanism is falsified if conditioning a slow fundamental composite on observable liquidity regimes does not improve its six-day information coefficient or reduces it after trading-cost assumptions."""

from __future__ import annotations

import numpy as np
import pandas as pd

from quant_fund_agent.factors.base import BaseFactor
from quant_fund_agent.factors.ops import rank
from quant_fund_agent.factors.registry import register_factor


def _cross_sectional_median(frame: pd.DataFrame) -> pd.Series:
    """Robust market aggregate available contemporaneously on each bar."""
    return frame.median(axis=1, skipna=True)


def _liquidity_regime_multiplier(
    close: pd.DataFrame,
    high: pd.DataFrame,
    low: pd.DataFrame,
    volume: pd.DataFrame,
) -> pd.DataFrame:
    """Causal smoothed liquidity-stress multiplier broadcast across names.

    Stress combines robust median range-per-volume, cross-sectional volume
    dispersion, and cross-sectional return dispersion.  Its 20-bar trailing
    z-score is passed through a bounded logistic function, preventing a single
    market shock from creating unstable exposure changes.
    """
    safe_close = close.replace(0.0, np.nan)
    safe_volume = volume.replace(0.0, np.nan)

    intraday_range = ((high - low).abs() / safe_close).replace([np.inf, -np.inf], np.nan)
    range_per_volume = intraday_range / safe_volume
    market_impact = _cross_sectional_median(range_per_volume)
    impact_log = np.log1p(market_impact.clip(lower=0.0))

    log_volume = np.log1p(volume.clip(lower=0.0))
    volume_dispersion = log_volume.std(axis=1, skipna=True)

    returns = close.pct_change().replace([np.inf, -np.inf], np.nan)
    return_dispersion = returns.std(axis=1, skipna=True)

    def trailing_zscore(series: pd.Series, window: int) -> pd.Series:
        mean = series.rolling(window, min_periods=10).mean()
        std = series.rolling(window, min_periods=10).std().replace(0.0, np.nan)
        return ((series - mean) / std).clip(lower=-4.0, upper=4.0)

    stress_raw = (
        trailing_zscore(impact_log, 20).fillna(0.0)
        + trailing_zscore(volume_dispersion, 20).fillna(0.0)
        + trailing_zscore(return_dispersion, 20).fillna(0.0)
    ) / 3.0

    smoothed_stress = stress_raw.ewm(halflife=5, adjust=False, min_periods=1).mean()
    defensive_tilt = 1.0 / (1.0 + np.exp(-smoothed_stress.clip(-4.0, 4.0)))

    # Preserve a meaningful base quality exposure in benign markets while
    # increasing the importance of resilience during stressed liquidity states.
    multiplier = 0.75 + 0.50 * defensive_tilt
    return pd.DataFrame(
        np.broadcast_to(multiplier.to_numpy()[:, None], close.shape),
        index=close.index,
        columns=close.columns,
    )


@register_factor
class StableFactorRegimeLiquidityTimingTilt(BaseFactor):
    """Liquidity-regime-conditioned quality and balance-sheet resilience tilt."""

    factor_id = "stable_factor_regime_liquidity_timing_tilt"
    name = "Liquidity-Regime Factor Timing Tilt"
    category = "other"
    description = (
        "A slow cross-sectional quality, resilience, and conservative-investment "
        "composite whose defensive balance-sheet component is amplified by a "
        "causal smoothed market liquidity-stress regime based on range-per-volume, "
        "volume dispersion, and return dispersion."
    )
    window_length = 40
    inputs = [
        "close",
        "high",
        "low",
        "volume",
        "roe",
        "roic",
        "incomeQuality",
        "debtToEquity",
        "cashRatio",
        "assetGrowth",
    ]
    prediction_horizon = 6
    suggested_horizons = [6]

    def calc(self, data: dict[str, pd.DataFrame]) -> pd.DataFrame:
        close = data["close"]
        high = data["high"].reindex_like(close)
        low = data["low"].reindex_like(close)
        volume = data["volume"].reindex_like(close)

        roe = data["roe"].reindex_like(close)
        roic = data["roic"].reindex_like(close)
        income_quality = data["incomeQuality"].reindex_like(close)
        debt_to_equity = data["debtToEquity"].reindex_like(close)
        cash_ratio = data["cashRatio"].reindex_like(close)
        asset_growth = data["assetGrowth"].reindex_like(close)

        # Fundamental data are point-in-time quarterly step functions.  Row-wise
        # ranks retain the slow public information while avoiding arbitrary level
        # comparisons across sectors and accounting scales.
        profitability = (rank(roe) + rank(roic) + rank(income_quality)) / 3.0
        resilience = (rank(-debt_to_equity) + rank(cash_ratio)) / 2.0
        conservative_investment = rank(-asset_growth)

        base_quality = (
            0.50 * profitability
            + 0.25 * resilience
            + 0.25 * conservative_investment
        )

        regime_multiplier = _liquidity_regime_multiplier(close, high, low, volume)

        # In stressed markets, explicitly favor resilient balance sheets over the
        # more cyclically sensitive profitability and investment sleeves.
        stress_share = (regime_multiplier - 0.75) / 0.50
        conditioned = (
            (1.0 - 0.20 * stress_share) * base_quality
            + (0.20 * stress_share) * resilience
        ) * regime_multiplier

        return rank(conditioned).fillna(0.5)

"""When a stock's absolute returns abruptly become synchronized with its sector, the sector is likely experiencing a common information or deleveraging episode rather than unrelated idiosyncratic noise. A constituent that has materially lagged the sector's signed move despite joining its volatility regime may be a delayed price-discovery receiver and should catch up. The signal should fail when synchronization increases but lagging members do not subsequently close their sector-relative return gaps."""

from __future__ import annotations

import numpy as np
import pandas as pd

from quant_fund_agent.factors.base import BaseFactor
from quant_fund_agent.factors.ops import rank
from quant_fund_agent.factors.registry import register_factor


def _leave_one_out_sector_median(
    panel: pd.DataFrame, labels: pd.Series
) -> pd.DataFrame:
    """Return each column's leave-one-out sector median, row by row.

    The implementation uses sorted cross-sections and inverse sort positions,
    avoiding a per-security Python loop while preserving exact leave-one-out
    medians in sectors of arbitrary size. Missing observations are excluded.
    """
    values = np.asarray(panel, dtype=float)
    output = np.full(values.shape, np.nan, dtype=float)

    for _, members in labels.groupby(labels, sort=False).groups.items():
        positions = panel.columns.get_indexer(members)
        if len(positions) < 2:
            continue

        group_values = values[:, positions]
        valid = np.isfinite(group_values)
        valid_count = valid.sum(axis=1, keepdims=True)

        sortable = np.where(valid, group_values, np.inf)
        order = np.argsort(sortable, axis=1)
        sorted_values = np.take_along_axis(sortable, order, axis=1)
        inverse_order = np.argsort(order, axis=1)

        remaining_count = valid_count - 1
        lower_remaining = (remaining_count - 1) // 2
        upper_remaining = remaining_count // 2

        lower_original = lower_remaining + (inverse_order <= lower_remaining)
        upper_original = upper_remaining + (inverse_order <= upper_remaining)
        lower_original = np.clip(lower_original, 0, len(positions) - 1)
        upper_original = np.clip(upper_original, 0, len(positions) - 1)

        lower_value = np.take_along_axis(sorted_values, lower_original, axis=1)
        upper_value = np.take_along_axis(sorted_values, upper_original, axis=1)
        loo_median = 0.5 * (lower_value + upper_value)

        usable = valid & (valid_count >= 2)
        output[:, positions] = np.where(usable, loo_median, np.nan)

    return pd.DataFrame(output, index=panel.index, columns=panel.columns)


def _rolling_beta_and_residual(
    stock_return: pd.DataFrame,
    sector_return: pd.DataFrame,
    window: int,
    min_periods: int,
) -> tuple[pd.DataFrame, pd.DataFrame]:
    """Causal rolling OLS beta and contemporaneous residual for y = beta * x."""
    mean_stock = stock_return.rolling(window, min_periods=min_periods).mean()
    mean_sector = sector_return.rolling(window, min_periods=min_periods).mean()
    mean_cross = (stock_return * sector_return).rolling(
        window, min_periods=min_periods
    ).mean()
    mean_sector_sq = (sector_return * sector_return).rolling(
        window, min_periods=min_periods
    ).mean()

    covariance = mean_cross - mean_stock * mean_sector
    variance = mean_sector_sq - mean_sector * mean_sector
    beta = (covariance / variance.replace(0.0, np.nan)).clip(-5.0, 5.0)
    residual = stock_return - beta * sector_return
    return beta, residual


@register_factor
class SectorVolatilitySynchronizationCatchup(BaseFactor):
    """Catch-up signal for stocks joining an accelerating sector volatility regime."""

    factor_id = "sector_volatility_sync_residual_catchup"
    name = "Sector Volatility Synchronization Catch-Up"
    category = "statistical_arbitrage"
    description = (
        "Ranks stocks with an abrupt increase in correlation between their absolute "
        "returns and leave-one-out sector volatility, scaled by their signed "
        "sector-beta residual catch-up gap."
    )
    window_length = 60
    inputs = ["close", "sector"]
    prediction_horizon = 6
    suggested_horizons = [6]

    def calc(self, data: dict[str, pd.DataFrame]) -> pd.DataFrame:
        close = data["close"].replace([np.inf, -np.inf], np.nan)
        sector_labels = data["sector"].iloc[0]

        stock_return = close.pct_change(fill_method=None).replace(
            [np.inf, -np.inf], np.nan
        )
        abs_return = stock_return.abs()

        loo_abs_sector_return = _leave_one_out_sector_median(
            abs_return, sector_labels
        )
        loo_sector_return = _leave_one_out_sector_median(
            stock_return, sector_labels
        )

        # Short versus long trailing correlations isolate an abrupt common-volatility
        # transition rather than a permanently high-correlation sector constituent.
        sync_short = abs_return.rolling(20, min_periods=15).corr(
            loo_abs_sector_return
        )
        sync_long = abs_return.rolling(60, min_periods=40).corr(
            loo_abs_sector_return
        )
        synchronization_acceleration = (sync_short - sync_long).clip(lower=0.0)
        synchronization_strength = sync_short.clip(lower=0.0)
        activation = synchronization_acceleration * synchronization_strength

        beta, residual = _rolling_beta_and_residual(
            stock_return, loo_sector_return, 40, 25
        )
        residual_scale = residual.rolling(40, min_periods=25).std().replace(
            0.0, np.nan
        )

        # Construct the gap in the sector move's direction, then restore the
        # trade direction. This equals beta * sector return - stock return,
        # i.e. the return required for the lagging security to catch up.
        sector_direction = np.sign(loo_sector_return)
        directional_participation_gap = sector_direction * (
            beta * loo_sector_return - stock_return
        )
        catchup_return = sector_direction * directional_participation_gap
        standardized_catchup = catchup_return / residual_scale

        score = (activation * standardized_catchup).where(activation > 0.0)
        return rank(score).replace([np.inf, -np.inf], np.nan).fillna(0.0)

"""A large directional close within a wide daily range is more likely to represent durable information when it is achieved with unusually little volume, because informed traders can move a thin order book before broader participation arrives. Conversely, a large range requiring exceptional volume but ending near the middle of the bar is more consistent with two-sided inventory transfer and should not receive the same continuation attribution. The signal is killed if low-participation directional range expansions reverse as often as high-participation, low-efficiency bars; persistence arises because daily-bar participants infer information content only gradually."""

from __future__ import annotations

import numpy as np
import pandas as pd

from quant_fund_agent.factors.base import BaseFactor
from quant_fund_agent.factors.ops import rank
from quant_fund_agent.factors.registry import register_factor


def _causal_robust_winsorize(
    values: pd.DataFrame, lookback: int, min_periods: int
) -> pd.DataFrame:
    """Causally cap each name at its trailing 5th and 95th percentiles."""
    clean = values.replace([np.inf, -np.inf], np.nan)
    rolling = clean.rolling(lookback, min_periods=min_periods)
    lower = rolling.quantile(0.05)
    upper = rolling.quantile(0.95)
    capped = clean.clip(lower=lower, upper=upper)
    return clean.where(lower.isna() | upper.isna(), capped)


@register_factor
class RangeVolumeInformationEfficiencyGap(BaseFactor):
    """Directional abnormal range per unit of relative volume."""

    factor_id = "range_volume_information_efficiency_gap"
    name = "Range-Volume Information Efficiency Gap"
    category = "microstructure"
    description = (
        "Compute directional close location within the high-low range, scaled by "
        "abnormal range and divided by relative volume after robust winsorization. "
        "Favor strong signed close-location moves with high range-per-unit-volume "
        "and penalize bars whose close is near the intrabar midpoint."
    )
    window_length = 60
    inputs = ["high", "low", "close", "volume"]
    prediction_horizon = 6
    suggested_horizons = [6]

    def calc(self, data: dict[str, pd.DataFrame]) -> pd.DataFrame:
        high = data["high"]
        low = data["low"]
        close = data["close"]
        volume = data["volume"]

        valid_price = high.notna() & low.notna() & close.notna() & (close.abs() > 0.0)
        valid_volume = volume.notna() & (volume > 0.0)
        valid = valid_price & valid_volume

        bar_range = (high - low).where(valid_price)
        normalized_range = (bar_range / close.abs().replace(0.0, np.nan)).replace(
            [np.inf, -np.inf], np.nan
        )
        safe_range = _causal_robust_winsorize(normalized_range, 60, 20)

        # A rolling median gives a slow, robust estimate of normal daily range.
        typical_range = safe_range.rolling(40, min_periods=20).median().replace(0.0, np.nan)
        abnormal_range = (safe_range / typical_range).replace([np.inf, -np.inf], np.nan)
        abnormal_range = _causal_robust_winsorize(abnormal_range, 60, 20)

        safe_volume = _causal_robust_winsorize(volume.where(valid_volume), 60, 20)
        typical_volume = safe_volume.rolling(40, min_periods=20).median().replace(0.0, np.nan)
        relative_volume = (safe_volume / typical_volume).replace([np.inf, -np.inf], np.nan)

        # Prevent a residual zero-volume observation from creating an unbounded score.
        relative_volume = relative_volume.clip(lower=0.10)

        # This is +1 at the high, -1 at the low, and zero at the intrabar midpoint.
        close_location = (
            (2.0 * close - high - low) / bar_range.replace(0.0, np.nan)
        ).clip(lower=-1.0, upper=1.0)

        efficiency_gap = (close_location * abnormal_range / relative_volume).replace(
            [np.inf, -np.inf], np.nan
        )
        efficiency_gap = _causal_robust_winsorize(efficiency_gap, 60, 20).where(valid)

        signal = rank(efficiency_gap)
        return signal.where(valid, 0.5).fillna(0.5)
